The proposition removes the qualification “I don’t really think.” Having “much to do with AGI” supplies no shared criterion for testing the claim.

entries.test: Public comparative evaluations of GPT-4 and its predecessors would show whether they exhibit the same qualitative capabilities and failure modes.
entries.note: The surrounding examples clarify the comparison; qualitative sameness does not require identical benchmark scores.

entries.test: Published GPT-4 evaluations and reproducible examples would establish whether hallucinations, unreliable answers, and complex-planning failures persisted at publication.
entries.note: Marcus endorses the planning limitation even while noting the paper's authors acknowledge it.

entries.test: The two papers and contemporaneous public disclosures would establish what was revealed about GPT-4, including its architecture and training data.
entries.note: The source says absolutely nothing about the model has been revealed; the proposition narrows that assertion to architecture and training data in the papers.

entries.test: Public research methods and independent evaluations would establish whether rigorous tests of the paper's general-intelligence claim can be conducted without access to GPT-4's training data.
entries.note: Marcus asserts the testing limitation in his own voice; he does not endorse the embedded general-intelligence claim.

entries.test: OpenAI's published training practices and independent tests using demonstrably fresh cases would establish whether incorporating user experiments prevents valid generalization testing.
entries.note: Davis is credited as a source, but Marcus adopts and asserts the claim himself.

entries.test: Contemporaneous deployment records, capability and reliability evaluations, risk disclosures, and published safety measures would establish the systems' capabilities, failures, risks, and available constraints.
entries.note: The claim has a practical reading grounded in deployed products and disclosed safety practices.

entries.test: Public evidence of model access and effective risk-reduction measures available to independent researchers, regulators, or other parties would test whether opacity leaves only Microsoft and OpenAI able to address these risks.
entries.note: The assertion that only these companies can do anything about the risks is a firm, testable exclusivity claim.
In context, this demands a change rather than predicting that deployment will end.

entries.test: Contemporaneous deployment figures, company risk disclosures, review records, and proposed mitigations would establish mass deployment, the reviewability of claims, and whether substantive solutions were outlined.
entries.note: The proposition drops the assertions that the claims are extravagant and unreviewed. Potential risk describes the deployed products; the sentence also makes concrete assertions about existing disclosures and mitigations.
The condition governs a recommendation to contemplate shutdown, not a forecast that shutdown will occur.
